terms.grammar: phrase, with the genitive of a gerund or the dative
evidence: Cic. Sest. 136: dīcendī fīnem facere (Lewis & Short)
Verg. A. 3.718: factōque hīc fīne quiēvit
terms.comment: dīcendī fīnem faciam, I’ll stop talking; with the dative, fīnem injūriīs factūrum (Caes. BG 1.33.1).

terms.gloss: end, finish, put an end to
terms.comment: Its first sense is to mark the limits of something (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: sīc pater Aenēās intentīs omnibus ūnus fāta renarrābat dīvum cursūsque docēbat. conticuit tandem factōque hīc fīne quiēvit
phrases.english: So father Aeneas alone, with all of them listening, told again of the fates the gods had sent and taught them his wanderings. At last he fell silent, made an end here, and rested.

phrases.latin: haec quae Pīcēnīs venit subducta trapētīs inchoat atque eadem fīnit olīva dapēs
phrases.english: this olive, fresh from the Picene presses, begins the meal, and the same olive ends it
but you’ll let me finish my game

sources: Lewis & Short: finis · Lewis & Short: finio
